recipes.name: Anytime Canned Corn Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch salt and ground black pepper

steps.text: Whisk together the apple cider vinegar, sugar, olive oil, water, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Add the corn, green and red bell peppers, onion, and tomato, and lightly toss. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Anytime Canned Corn Salad
raw_recipe.description: This canned corn salad recipe makes a bright and colorful side dish that's perfect for picnics or potlucks because it's easy to make and has no mayo.

review.reviewBody: This is my submission--I suppose it's not great to rate your own recipe, but I made this tonight and tried some new things with it--was great and wanted to share the ideas. Tonight, I used 1 Tblsp sugar and 1 Tblsp Splenda, with 2 Tblsp cider vinegar and 1 Tblsp rice wine vinegar. This is the amount of sweetness we like in it, but some like it a little less sweet so adjust to your own taste. Also, for tonight, I used a can of Summer Crisp Mexicorn (I think its called Southwestern, actually) that had red and green peppers and black beans in it. Added a can of rinsed great northern beans also. Was REALLY good with the beans, added protein and fiber. Thanks to all who have reviewed--it helps to get feedback. I appreciate that, and I'm glad you liked the salad.

Delish! I used fresh corn off the cob(cooked and cooled) we had left from dinner, added parsley, a pinch of garlic powder and green onions. I didn't use the apple cider vinegar, but did use regular distilled. I omitted the water, but honestly ... don't think you could ruin this. I didn't measure anything and it was perfect!

Made as is, and both myself and my husband really enjoyed it! Oh, wait! I used Frozen corn instead of the canned. Lol, I poured the corn into the bean can so I could have the right amount :P Thank you for sharing this simple but yummy recipe!

This is not really a fair rating of this recipe in particular but I found a recipe similiar to this at my local grocery store so I used this as a base for that salad. I added 1 can of drained and rinsed black beans, 1 can of drained and rinsed lima beans, an extra (smaller size) can of corn and whole wheat fusilli noodles. For the sauce I tried the one in this recipe and didn't really care for it so I added about 1/2 to 3/4 of a cup of roasted pepper salad dressing (similiar to italian), very yummy.
I like this because you can pick and choose veggies or stir-up the dressing according to your preferences. I used freshly cooked corn-on-cob and cut it off.
Made this today with fresh corn on the cob (cooked) and I did reduce the sugar to 1 tsp. Wow so yummy. I used red pepper and red onion!

I made this salad for family Sunday dinner and everyone loved it! It's crisp, light, tangy, and sweet. Very easy to make, thank you for that! I made it my own by using halved grape tomatoes and fresh basil from the garden, but made the dressing exactly as the recipe stood. Perfect ! I will definitely keep this in my repertoire.
Really good as written, I also added black beans (drained and rinsed), to give it a little more substance.

Very good fresh summer salad. Quick and easy recipes. I made this for a block party because I had a ton of vegetables I wanted to use and leftover corn on the cob. I cut the corn off of the cob and mixed all of the ingredients together. I topped the entire salad off with fresh parsley and added fresh grape tomatoes. Everyone loved the salad, however, I personally felt like something was missing. I will definitely make this again.
I followed the directions pretty closely except used freshly grilled corn on the cob (I cut the corn off). Also used all kinds of bell peppers, not just red/green. Tasty!

This is a great summer side dish. One note, I backed off on the sugar a bit the second time and thought it tasted better. The thing I like about this recipe is how easy it is to mix it up. Using corn as the base you can vary the recipe based on what is coming out of the garden and the vinegar really helps blend all the flavors together. The one thing I was surprised by was how well this kept in the fridge.

I will definitely make again. I doubled the vegetables but not the dressing, and reduced sugar by half. Maybe next time no sugar and add some diced cucumber. Great foundation recipe that will inspire changes.
This one is like one I have made this for years. It is al waysrequested
Loved it! My new favorite thing to make.
Crisp and fresh and hard to mess up!
IAadded black and green sliced olives-Excellent salad!

Great recipe serves as a base. I threw in some veggies that I had left over, like a can of artichoke hearts and finished off a bottle of Red Pepper vinaigrette. Sorry to those of you purists who want a recipe rated on exactly as it is written. My purpose was to use this as a guide for a salad to take to a pitch in and it was great for that. I like reading changes that other people make. I think it is interesting and provides some good ideas.
